### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, touching **27** documentable anchor(s).

**20** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json df22adc370bae67424297c3d00841ce7ca0d3365`.

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `os validate (command, 87 pages)`
- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **226** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **35** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json df22adc370bae67424297c3d00841ce7ca0d3365` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `53282d56b6aea5396240469ec80f55e5c6801854` — the merge of head `8c5e74a7b61a2eded18b13b6cfdded4838ba22ef` into base `df22adc370bae67424297c3d00841ce7ca0d3365`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 53282d56b6aea5396240469ec80f55e5c6801854 && git checkout 53282d56b6aea5396240469ec80f55e5c6801854
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin df22adc370bae67424297c3d00841ce7ca0d3365 8c5e74a7b61a2eded18b13b6cfdded4838ba22ef && git checkout -B drift-repro df22adc370bae67424297c3d00841ce7ca0d3365 && git merge --no-ff 8c5e74a7b61a2eded18b13b6cfdded4838ba22ef

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json df22adc370bae67424297c3d00841ce7ca0d3365
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs df22adc370bae67424297c3d00841ce7ca0d3365` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `8c5e74a7b61a2eded18b13b6cfdded4838ba22ef`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

- Face: consumer of a declared contract (`Clause-②: yes` on the claim, PR body and changeset). The diff reads `RestrictionProfileSchema` (`@objectstack/spec/system`, landed as item 1) and does not touch it: no path under `packages/spec/**`, no governed path, no route, no new error code. Diff read in full: 6 files, +929/−0.
- **Parse, never half a profile.** `loadRestrictionProfile` parses with the spec's own schema; an invalid profile, `{}`, non-JSON, a missing file or a URL is refused through the existing catch-all naming the issue path, before the stack is read. This honours the schema's own docblock ("a profile that omits a dimension is refused at parse") and Prime Directive 12 (no lenient consumer).
- **One vocabulary, no second list.** `allowCode` reads `hooks` (named by the profile docblock) plus every key `UNMANAGED_INSTALL_KEY_DISPOSITIONS` classifies `code`, gated by the same `unmanagedInstallValueCarries` test; node types read `FLOW_BUILTIN_NODE_TYPES` / `FLOW_STRUCTURAL_NODE_TYPES`; regions are walked with `collectFlowGraphs`. Each of these is the spec's exported reader, so a key or node type the spec gains moves the reader the same release.
- **Reader rules (review 6710350208 ③/④) implemented as ruled,** in `judgeNodeType`: (1) start/end return before any rule; (2) a type outside `FlowNodeAction` is allowed under `allowCode: true` and refused naming `allowCode` under `false`; (3) `script` under `allowCode: false` short-circuits to one `allowCode` row before the list is read. Every row carries exactly one `rule`. Pinned by unit cases and by the ablations in the report (rule 3 → 3 red, schedule check → 3 red, rule 1 → 5 red).
- **Version drift warns only.** `restrictionProfileVersionDrift` resolves from the config's directory (spec falls back to the CLI's own copy; skills has none and reports `local: null`). It rides `warnings`, appended last in `warningsSoFar()`, and is outside the list `--strict` gates — the protocol-drift advisory's precedent: the target's version is the environment's, not the stack's.
- **No `--target`, no change.** Every new step is behind `if (targetProfile)`; CONTROL pinned in-process (exit 0, no drift entry). The gate-parity ledger records `judgeRestrictionProfile` as validate-only (`os build` names no target) and the two readers as not-a-gate.

### ② Semver level

- A new optional flag and new rows only when the flag is passed ⇒ additive. Changeset `@objectstack/cli` patch (Metadata-protocol none) is the repo's grading for this level axis. No narrowing arm: no existing invocation refuses anything it accepted before.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Security/permission boundary: none moved. The command reads a local file and the stack; it writes nothing and fetches nothing (the URL form is refused, not guessed).
- Fail-closed edges declared, not hidden: `parallel` / `try_catch` (engine built-ins outside `FlowNodeAction`) and `devPlugins` are refused under `allowCode: false` by the one-table reading; the vocabulary fix belongs to spec → #31239. The URL form waits for cloud#3713 → #31240.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-6pkacq`
Reviewed-by: `session_017ihL2dLQEXWGsE2SZ3Qn5F`

**VERDICT: PASS**
